text:
alexa: heads up — getting customer escalations about timeouts + 5xx on hosted inference. p95 token latency jumped, and a few tenants hit `request queued too long` errors around 17:42 UTC. stack traces show gateway 502/504s.

maya_support: which tenant? any reproducible sample? customers report request hanging for ~12s then 504.

alexa: two tenants impacted, one commercial (brightpay) and internal canary. repro curl below from canary: 
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -H 'Authorization: Bearer $KEY' -d '{\"model\":\"gpt-redwood-0\",\"input\":\"hello\"}' -v
```
response: HTTP/1.1 504 Gateway Timeout after ~12s, body: `\{"error\":\"request queued too long\"}`

opsbot: incident-bot triggered alert: `hosted-gateway.queue_depth > 85%` (17:43:02 UTC).

jin_oncall: I'm looking at ingress dashboards now. Continuous batching backlog spike at 17:40 — queue depth climbed from 30% -> 92% over ~90s. batcher_kv_cache churn increased too.

sam_sre: any recent deploys or routing changes? could be a kernel selection regression or a quantized model cold path.

maya_support: customer says they didn't change traffic. traffic graph shows burst but within expected.

alexa: we had a small runtime deploy 17:38 for an optimization; rollout was partial but could correlate.

jin_oncall: grabbing traces. payloads look normal. most time spent waiting in request queue; dequeue latencies exploded. looks like prefix/KV cache spin-up for many concurrent longseq requests hitting slow path.

sam_sre: possible mitigation: enable short-circuit fallback to smaller model variant and bump queue-depth threshold to force early rejects for short time. also consider raising batcher concurrency.

maya_support: customer-facing note drafted: "We're actively investigating intermittent timeouts and 5xx errors for hosted inference — mitigation in progress."

alexa: action plan: 1) roll back 17:38 runtime change to canary nodes 2) temporarily increase `max_queue_depth` for hosted-gateway to 120% for 5m window 3) flip fallback to smaller model for affected tenants 4) collect a few representative requests.

jin_oncall: rolling back canary now. `kubectl -n runtime rollout undo deploy/rt-canary`

deploy-bot: deploy: rollback started for rt-canary by jin_oncall at 17:46:12 UTC.

sam_sre: I pushed a short-lived config bump: `hosted-gateway.queue.max_depth=120` (applied to us-west-1). monitors & autoscale in progress.

opsbot: autoscaler: added 2 nodes to pool (scale up) at 17:48:05 UTC.

jin_oncall: enabling model fallback routing for brightpay tenant via feature flag.

maya_support: customer replied: saw immediate improvement, one user reported success on retry. still seeing a few 5xxs but much reduced. :thumbsup:

alexa: collecting traces for last successful vs failed requests. please add any interesting spans to the thread.

sam_sre: attaching snippet of queue metrics (simplified): 
```
17:39:30 queue_depth=28%
17:40:10 queue_depth=47%
17:40:50 queue_depth=76%
17:41:20 queue_depth=92%  <-- backlog spike
17:42:00 dequeue_latency_p95=12000ms
17:46:00 queue_depth=35% after rollback/scale
```

jin_oncall: root cause hypothesis: deploy changed kernel selection heuristics causing cold-path KV cache loads to serialize, increasing dequeue time for longseqs and causing continuous-batching backlog to snowball (throttle-spiral).

maya_support: are there new short-term mitigations we should recommend customers do? e.g., reduce max input length or enable client-side retries with jitter.

sam_sre: recommend: 1) if possible, lower request concurrency client-side 2) add exponential backoff 3) pin to `gpt-redwood-0-small` fallback during incident

alexa: next steps: 1) postmortem ticket 2) add a kinetic guard to prevent kernel-selection rollouts during high queue_depth 3) build a circuit-breaker to early reject requests exceeding queue wait SLO.

jin_oncall: I'll keep the rollback active and monitor for 30m, collecting KV cache metrics and traces.

maya_support: customers updated. I'll keep support looped.

opsbot: incident-bot: alert resolved at 17:57:01 UTC (queue_depth < 70%).

alexa: thanks team. please add any follow-ups to the postmortem.

sam_sre: filing tracking issue: `runtime/kernel-heuristic-rollout-investigation` and adding changelog entry.

maya_support: will draft customer incident summary and ETA for full fix.

jin_oncall: note for postmortem: reproduce by simulating many concurrent longseq requests right after a cold-start/prefix-cache eviction to observe dequeue amplification.

alexa: end of thread for now — reopening if we see regressions.
